II

The listening ritual

The board does part of the remembering.

“After each move, take your hand away from the piece and allow the new position to settle.”

Chess Archived is paced for a real board and real hands. Coordinates tell you where a piece is. Spoken move numbers tell you where you are in the story. Board checkpoints let you recover without beginning again.

The spoiler shield

The physical system · No special board required

Three familiar objects. One new protocol.

Any coordinate chessboard, a simple audio player, and two coded move strips are enough to reopen a great game.

▱Screen-freeStay present. No distractions.
▣Spoiler-freeThe story unfolds by position.
↻ReplayableA different seat changes the game.

III

Experience editions

One game. Six honest ways to enter it.

Identity, history, and chess context are separate spoiler controls. Each edition reveals a different amount, from total mystery to a complete historical masterclass.

  1. 01

    Pure Mystery

    No names, year, event, opening, or result. Meet the position before the legend.

    Most immersive
  2. 02

    Play as White

    Take White’s seat. Black’s ideas appear only as they would across the board.

    First person
  3. 03

    Play as Black

    Enter the same game from the other chair and inherit a different set of problems.

    Reverse seat
  4. 04

    Historical Room

    Enter the era and tournament while the players themselves remain unknown.

    Period context
  5. 05

    Player Mystery

    Know the two names, but not which color each controls. Let style become evidence.

    Identity puzzle
  6. 06

    Complete Masterclass

    Names, colors, era, opening, alternatives, sources, patterns, and the full reveal.

    Full context

Inside archive CA—001 · In listener testing

Every square is treated as part of the story.

The first archive reconstructs a complete historical game. Every legal move, spoken origin, destination square, check status, and final board state has been audited. Rendered pacing and blind physical-board testing remain underway.
